newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent stalled by $18.62/77 gap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent stalled by $18.62/77 gap.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

+ IPE Brent seen as stuck in range, with June's failure to breach key $18.62/77 gap seen as increasingly bearish. + Support for June seen at $18.20, $18 and then around last week's lows at $18.81 and $18.61. + Gas oil was expected to continue consolidation. Support for the contract seen around $169.00/50 in line with gap.
IPE Brent futures were expected to drift along in range on Friday, but some chartists said the fact June Brent had failed to close the $18.62/77 gap was becoming an increasingly bearish sign.
Also, few players expected any large moves higher while European players remained scarce as the continent extended the Thursday's Day holiday into the weekend.
June IPE Brent closed 23 cents lower at $18.29 a barrel on Thursday, while May gas ended 75 cents lower at $171.00 a tonne.
June Brent has so far failed to close the downside gap between $18.62 and $18.77 left on April 2-3.
That was seen as increasingly bearish by a number of chartists.
"We need to fill the gap for the market to turn positive, but judging by the action of the last few days people are still willing to sell below there," said Steve Kwan at MMS in London.
For many, the contract's failure to jump the technical hurdle was a sign of the fragility of the recent uptrend.

"Momentum has been bullish over the last fews days but Brent has failed to push higher which technically isn't very good," said Kwan. He added there was a good chance Brent could revisit the $17-$18 price band.
Kwan saw downside targets of $17.81 and $17.61 in line with the lows of April 23 and 17.

A number of chartists noted support above there around the $18.20 level in line with a hub of price activity over the past few days, with Relative Strength Indices suggesting the market approaching overbought levels.
The 14-day RSI stood at 59.66 percent at Thursday's close. Levels above 70 percent indicate the market is overbought, while levels under 30 percent that it is oversold.
Gas oil was also expected to spend the session range trading with a slightly negative bias.

Although gaps tend to have less significance on the gas oil chart because they are not that rare an occurrence, some chartists saw support for the May contract at around $169.00/50 in line with a gap left by the sessions of April 29 and 30.
